headline: E-orange Chief Advisor Masukur Rahman arrested in Dhaka
summary: The fugitive convict faces a six-month prison sentence in a fraud case and at least two dozen other legal charges.
details: Police arrested Masukur Rahman, the chief adviser and director of e-commerce platform E-orange, during a raid in the Kotwali area of Dhaka this morning.
Masukur was a fugitive convict who had been sentenced to six months' imprisonment in a fraud case filed with Gulshan Police Station.
DMP Assistant Commissioner Shah Mostafa Tarikuzzaman confirmed the arrest, stating it was carried out based on a tip-off.
Beyond the current conviction, police revealed that Masukur faces at least two dozen other cases across various police stations on charges of fraud and other offences.
He is expected to be produced before a Dhaka court tomorrow.
caption:
A fugitive convict and E-orange chief advisor arrested in Dhaka.

He faces a 6-month prison sentence and over 24 other fraud cases.

Police arrested Masukur Rahman, the chief adviser and director of e-commerce platform E-orange, during a raid in the Kotwali area of Dhaka this morning.

Masukur was a fugitive convict who had been sentenced to six months' imprisonment in a fraud case filed with Gulshan Police Station.

DMP Assistant Commissioner Shah Mostafa Tarikuzzaman confirmed the arrest, stating it was carried out based on a tip-off.

Beyond the current conviction, police revealed that Masukur faces at least two dozen other cases across various police stations on charges of fraud and other offences.

He is expected to be produced before a Dhaka court tomorrow.

headline_marked: US Supreme Court [[blocks Trump's bid to restrict birthright citizenship]]
headline: US Supreme Court blocks Trump's bid to restrict birthright citizenship
summary: The top court ruled that the 14th Amendment guarantees citizenship to virtually anyone born in the US, rejecting a priority immigration crackdown by Donald Trump.
details: The US Supreme Court rejected President Donald Trump's attempt to restrict birthright citizenship on the final day of its annual term, ruling that such a move would violate the US Constitution.
Chief Justice John Roberts stated that the 14th Amendment guarantees citizenship to virtually anyone born in the United States, with only a few narrow exceptions.
Trump's directive had sought to deny citizenship to children born in the US if neither parent was a citizen or legal permanent resident.
Experts had estimated that this restriction could have affected the legal status of as many as 250,000 babies born each year.
In a separate ruling, the court allowed states to ban transgender student athletes from women's sports teams, deciding 9-0 that such laws do not violate the Title IX civil rights statute.
The court also sided with Republican challengers to strike down federal limits on coordinated spending between political parties and candidates ahead of the midterm elections.
The Supreme Court currently maintains a 6-3 conservative majority, including three Trump appointees.
caption:
A major blow to Trump's immigration plan: The US Supreme Court has blocked his attempt to end birthright citizenship.

The US Supreme Court rejected President Donald Trump's attempt to restrict birthright citizenship on the final day of its annual term, ruling that such a move would violate the US Constitution.

Chief Justice John Roberts stated that the 14th Amendment guarantees citizenship to virtually anyone born in the United States, with only a few narrow exceptions.

Trump's directive had sought to deny citizenship to children born in the US if neither parent was a citizen or legal permanent resident.

Experts had estimated that this restriction could have affected the legal status of as many as 250,000 babies born each year.

In a separate ruling, the court allowed states to ban transgender student athletes from women's sports teams, deciding 9-0 that such laws do not violate the Title IX civil rights statute.

The court also sided with Republican challengers to strike down federal limits on coordinated spending between political parties and candidates ahead of the midterm elections.

The Supreme Court currently maintains a 6-3 conservative majority, including three Trump appointees.
